newsitem.title: USA: U.S., state governments crack down on travel scams.
newsitem.headline: U.S., state governments crack down on travel scams.

text.p: Federal and state governments cracked down on travel fraud Thursday, taking coordinated legal action.

"Travel related scams are taking off again," the Federal Trade Commission said in announcing "Operation Trip-up," which includes both civil court actions and warnings to consumers on ways to avoid getting taken.
FTC consumer fraud director Jodie Bernstein said at a news conference the agency was pursuing five firms that allegedly had taken the public for $43 million in recent years.
But Bernstein also cautioned consumers to be wary in making travel and vacation-related purchases, because travel fraud runs into the billions of dollars each year.
She said one way to avoid fraud is to buy vacations and travel with credit cards, providing some recourse later if promised services are not provided.

"Buy vacation travel only from a business you know, get the details of your vacation and any refund policy in writing before you pay, and be wary of pre-paying for multiple years worth of travel," Bernstein said.

One scam targeted immigrants and promised "affordable" tickets to their homes in India or Africa. The merchant, "Your Travels and Tours" of Cambridge, Mass., required cash payment immediately, the government alleged.

One of those who lost money from "Your Travels" was Aatif Aaquil of Detroit, Mich., who purchased tickets to visit family in Patna, India over the winter 1996 holidays. He never got a ticket, despite repeated phone calls.
"Since then I've been asking for the refund of my money," he told the news conference. "I paid them something like $2,990 and I haven't received a single dollar back as yet."

The government received more complaints about Design Travel of Santa Rosa, Calif., than any about any other firm. FTC lawyer Collot Guerard charged that bank records show it processed $14 million in credit cards, falsely promising "free vacations."
People paid Design Travel $600 to $900 for a ferry ride from Florida to the Bahamas for a stay in a vermin-infested hotel, Guerard alleged.
The federal government also cracked down on Gold Crown Express, Worldwide Vacation Services and William Ernest Taft.
The firm operated in various states and allegedly claimed it could sell American timeshares in Europe. Bernstein said there is no market for the timeshares anywhere.

World Class Network of Irvine, Calif., allegedly sold so-called "tutorial" kits for people to operate "home-based travel agencies" that supposedly gave people a way of getting low-priced tickets. They don't.
Travel Bahamas Tours of Florida and Texas allegedly sold pre-paid certificates for pre-paid stays at world class hotels, but the hotels had never heard of the firm.

State attorneys general in California, Connecticut, Florida, Illinois, Massachusetts, Michigan, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Vermont, Washington and Wisconsin joined in on targeting the travel fraud, going after some of the same firms as the federal government, as well as others.
